nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of integers with $|A| < 6$. Then $|A + A| \le |A - A|$, where $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$ is the sumset and $A - A = \{a - b : a, b \in A\}$ is the difference set of $A$.
nodes.title: Chu's theorem for arbitrary finite sets of integers

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of nonnegative integers with $|A| < 6$. Then $|A + A| \le |A - A|$, where $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$ is the sumset and $A - A = \{a - b : a, b \in A\}$ is the difference set of $A$; that is, $A$ is not sum-dominant.
nodes.title: Chu's theorem: sets with fewer than six elements are not sum-dominant
